# Pyth wire fixture

`accumulator.bin` is the decoded hexadecimal accumulator fixture in
[`wire.rs` at the pinned Pyth revision](https://github.com/pyth-network/pyth-crosschain/blob/918664828173a60a2cde1f8431474efb02a6b75f/pythnet/pythnet_sdk/src/wire.rs#L488).
The original Apache-2.0 notice and license are retained here. These fixtures are
excluded from the published library archive.

The other three files are its VAA, verification payload and first price message.
They were extracted by executing the pinned Dart parsers with networking denied.
The transfer is 1,291 bytes; its 952-byte VAA contains 13 signatures, guardian set
4, emitter chain 26 and sequence 123,319,103. Its verification payload starts with
`AUWV` and has 37 bytes. The first price message has 85 bytes and 12 proof hashes.

The Dart `parsePythWormholeMessage` helper rejects that real verification payload
as an unsupported version 65. Rust's production parser follows the official
message magic, variant, slot, ring size and root rather than that synthetic
version/kind envelope. Unit and portable cases use these original bytes, not
output generated by the Rust implementation under test.

## Account vectors

`legacy-price.bin` is the 432-byte two-publisher fixture produced by
`buildPriceAccount` in the pinned Dart repository's `price_account_test.dart`.
Its SHA256 is `6c7e42ce1e567144d3f6d260ec06b9a2728344f467b65aedad1ff7551c8020c8`.
That test source matches Dart revision `0138bb956d2d81ccc0c56edc602401c0df2f2b46`.
The Dart MIT notice is retained at the crate root.

`price-update-full.bin` and `price-update-partial.bin` are synthetic Borsh vectors
encoded independently in Dart with the receiver's field order. They use the same
prices and maximum unsigned confidence values. Their lengths are 133 and 134
bytes. The pinned Dart decoder accepts the partial account but rejects the full
account with `Data is too short (133 bytes) to be a PriceUpdateV2 account`.
Rust accepts both actual variant sizes and preserves optional account padding.

The primary receiver definition is
[`price_update.rs` at the pinned Pyth revision](https://github.com/pyth-network/pyth-crosschain/blob/918664828173a60a2cde1f8431474efb02a6b75f/target_chains/solana/pyth_solana_receiver_sdk/src/price_update.rs#L19-L59).
These account vectors are separate from the upstream Apache-2.0 transfer fixture
above. They contain fixed synthetic values and establish no cluster execution.

## Hermes response

`hermes-update.json` is a synthetic response independently decoded by the pinned
Dart `HermesPriceUpdate.fromJson` implementation. Its price and confidence exceed
128 bits, its publication time is the maximum signed 64 bit integer, and its slot
exceeds the exact range of a JavaScript number. The EMA uses integer JSON tokens,
including the negative confidence accepted by the reference model. The parser
preserves recorded components without assigning them price authenticity.

The reference execution also captures the three GET routes, eleven asset filter
names, two encodings, defaults, header precedence and retryable status classes.
Its source is the MIT-licensed Dart package at revision
`0138bb956d2d81ccc0c56edc602401c0df2f2b46`. The JSON values above are synthetic and
were not generated by the Rust implementation under test.

## Receiver instruction vectors

`receiver-atomic.bin`, `receiver-atomic-override.bin`, `receiver-posted.bin` and
`receiver-posted-override.bin` are complete instruction data emitted by executing
the pinned Dart builders. They use `vaa.bin` above, the synthetic message
`[9, 8, 7]` and two 20-byte proof hashes filled with `0xa1` and `0xa2`.
Default vectors use treasury zero; override vectors use treasury 255. The atomic
data has 1,016 bytes and posted data has 60 bytes, including their discriminators.
The Dart receipt separately retains all seven account addresses and roles,
program/authority overrides and default/custom PDA boundaries.

The VAA retains its upstream fixture provenance and Apache-2.0 notice above.
The instruction construction reference is the MIT-licensed Dart package at the
same pinned revision. These vectors establish serialization and metadata parity,
without guardian verification, transaction submission or cluster execution.
